seo.title: Boston homeless help and services - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified Boston help for people experiencing homelessness: shelter, meals, showers, health care, benefits, work, documents, legal aid, and specialist support.

page.heading: Boston — help for people experiencing homelessness
page.urgent: Medical, fire, or immediate danger: 911 Shelter and city services: 311 or 617-635-4500 Adult shelter referral: 617-534-4440 Families with children or a pregnant household member: 866-584-0653
page.notice: Beds, hours, meals, addresses, and eligibility can change. Call before a long trip. No listing guarantees a bed, meal, payment, treatment, benefit, or job on the same day. Call 911 for immediate danger or a life-threatening medical problem.
page.intro: If you need a safe place tonight, call the shelter before traveling or contact 311. Tell staff your age, gender identity, whether you are with children, whether anyone is pregnant, your accessibility or medical needs, and whether you have a pet. You may ask for help even if your identification is missing.
page.footer: No Home Help is not an emergency service and does not control beds. Always confirm before traveling.

entries.title: 911 — immediate danger or medical emergency
entries.description:
Call: 911.
Use 911 for trouble breathing, severe chest pain, unconsciousness, seizure, serious bleeding, suspected overdose, fire, violence in progress, or another immediate threat. Give the exact location and a nearby landmark.
When to call 911 — City of Boston

entries.title: BOS:311 — non-emergency city help
entries.description:
Call: 311 inside Boston or 617-635-4500.
Ask for the current shelter, warming or cooling location, city outreach, or another local service. Tell the operator if a person cannot travel safely, uses a wheelchair, has children, or has a pet.
Boston 311

entries.title: Pine Street Inn Street Outreach
entries.description:
Outreach line published by the City: 866-633-0170.
Outreach teams engage people sleeping outside and connect them with shelter, health care, and housing. If there is immediate medical danger, call 911 instead. For a routine request, give a precise location, description, and time last seen.
Pine Street Inn Street Outreach

entries.title: Massachusetts 211 — statewide resource referrals
entries.description:
Call: 211, available 24 hours.
Ask for a nearby meal, shelter, clothing, benefits, domestic-violence service, or other human service. Confirm the provider's hours and entry rules before traveling.
Massachusetts 211

entries.title: Warming and cooling information
entries.description:
Call: 311 or 617-635-4500.
Ask for the current open warming or cooling location and its hours. Do not rely on an old address during a weather emergency. Tell 311 if a person cannot travel safely or needs an accessible option.
Boston Emergency Management

entries.title: When weather becomes a medical emergency
entries.description:
Call 911 for confusion, fainting, severe weakness, very hot or cold skin, difficulty breathing, or inability to wake. During extreme heat, seek shade and water; during severe cold, keep clothing dry and cover exposed skin while arranging indoor help.
City emergency information

entries.title: Southampton Street Shelter — men
entries.description:
Phone: 617-534-4440.
City emergency shelter for adult men. The City lists direct access without an Office of Housing Stability referral. Call first for the current intake time and capacity, and tell staff about mobility, medical, language, or safety needs.
Boston Homeless Services

entries.title: Woods-Mullen Shelter — women
entries.description:
Phone: 617-534-7100.
City emergency shelter for adult women. Direct walk-in access is listed, but beds remain limited. Call before traveling and explain any disability, medical, language, or safety need.
City shelter directory

entries.title: Pine Street Inn — men's shelter
entries.description:
Front-door triage: 617-892-9228. City directory: 617-892-9207.
Emergency shelter and triage for adult men. Triage hours are published as 9:30 a.m.–6 p.m. daily. Call for intake instructions; arriving does not guarantee a bed.
Pine Street front-door triage

entries.title: Pine Street Yawkey House — women's shelter
entries.description:
Phone: 617-892-9321.
Emergency shelter for adult women. Call to confirm intake, accessibility, and current capacity before traveling.
Boston shelter directory

entries.title: Pine Street Shattuck Shelter — men
entries.description:
Phone: 617-892-7917.
Emergency shelter for adult men. Call for the day's intake process and bed availability.
City shelter and day-service listings
entries.address: Address: 170 Morton Street, Jamaica Plain, MA 02130

entries.title: Boston Night Center — overnight indoor space
entries.description:
Phone: 857-296-0332. Hours listed by the City: 8:30 p.m.–6:30 a.m.
Overnight space for adults, but it does not provide beds. Call to confirm current access and capacity.
Boston Night Center listing

entries.title: Family Emergency Assistance — families and pregnancy
entries.description:
Call: 866-584-0653.
Massachusetts Emergency Assistance shelter is for eligible families with children and households that include a pregnant person. Call to speak with a Homeless Coordinator. Screening and documentation are required, and placement may not be in Boston.
Massachusetts emergency housing help

entries.title: Office of Housing Stability — prevent homelessness
entries.description:
Phone: 617-635-4200. Hours: Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–5 p.m.
Information and referrals for eviction prevention and housing stability. The office does not directly place individuals in emergency shelter. Outside office hours, call 311.
Office of Housing Stability

entries.title: St. Francis House — breakfast and lunch
entries.description:
Phone: 617-542-4211. Building hours: daily, 6:30 a.m.–3 p.m.; Wednesday closes at 2 p.m.
Breakfast 7–9 a.m. and lunch 11:30 a.m.–1 p.m., plus showers, clothing, mail, computers, health care, recovery, and employment help. Services may reach capacity.
St. Francis House — get help

entries.title: Women's Lunch Place — meals for women
entries.description:
Phone: 617-267-0200. Hours: Monday–Saturday, 7 a.m.–2 p.m.
Breakfast 8–10:30 a.m., lunch noon–2 p.m., and a takeaway dinner, with showers, laundry, clothing, health care, computers, phones, mail, advocacy, legal help, and employment support.
Women's Lunch Place — current services

entries.title: Rosie's Place — meals for women
entries.description:
Phone: 617-442-9322.
Weekday breakfast 7:30–9 a.m., lunch 11:30 a.m.–1 p.m., dinner 4:30–6:45 p.m.; weekend brunch 10:30 a.m.–noon and dinner 3:30–4:30 p.m. The current guide also lists showers, laundry, computers, pantry, advocacy, and shelter intake. Confirm holiday changes.
Rosie's Place current service guide

entries.title: Boston Rescue Mission — meals and pantry
entries.description:
Main phone: 617-338-9000; food questions: 617-446-3458.
The program publishes a food pantry Monday 2–3 p.m. and Saturday 2–3:30 p.m. Meal access may be connected to program or overnight guests; call before traveling.
Boston Rescue Mission nutrition program

entries.title: Haley House — soup kitchen and pantry
entries.description:
Phone: 617-236-8132.
The organization lists morning meals and a Thursday food pantry, but its published schedule contains different meal times in different sections. Call for the current breakfast, pantry, clothing, and shower schedule before traveling.
Haley House food and meal programs

entries.title: Project Bread FoodSource Hotline
entries.description:
Call: 800-645-8333.
Free help finding nearby food and applying for SNAP. Ask for a location open today and tell the counselor if you cannot cook or store food.
Project Bread FoodSource Hotline

entries.title: Greater Boston Food Bank locator
entries.description:
Search for food pantries and meal programs by ZIP code. Each partner has its own hours, geographic limits, and documents. Call the provider before traveling.
SNAP help: 617-598-5022.
Find food — Greater Boston Food Bank

categories.title: Showers, laundry, clothing, mail, and internet

entries.title: St. Francis House day shelter
entries.description:
Showers, toiletries, clothing, mail, identification help, computers, phones, meals, and case management. Open every day; arrive early and ask which services require a sign-up.
St. Francis House day services

entries.title: Women's Lunch Place
entries.description:
Showers, laundry, clothing, toiletries, mail, computers, phones, meals, advocacy, and health services for women. Open Monday–Saturday, 7 a.m.–2 p.m.
Women's Lunch Place help

entries.title: Rosie's Place day services
entries.description:
Showers, laundry, computers, phones, advocacy, meals, and other support for women. The overnight shelter uses a weekday morning lottery; ask staff for the current process.
Rosie's Place service guide

entries.title: Boston Public Library — computers, Wi-Fi, charging, and information
entries.description:
Libraries provide free Wi-Fi, public computers, charging, restrooms, and staff help finding information. Some computer use requires a library card or guest pass. Check the branch's current hours before traveling.
Boston Public Library locations

entries.title: Mail and document safety
entries.description:
St. Francis House and Women's Lunch Place publish mail support for eligible guests. Ask whether you may use the address for benefits or job applications, how long mail is held, and what is needed for collection. Keep photographs of important documents in a protected account when possible.
St. Francis House service details

entries.title: Boston Health Care for the Homeless — Jean Yawkey Place
entries.description:
Phone: 857-654-1605.
Primary and urgent health care for people experiencing homelessness. Published hours: Monday, Wednesday, and Friday 8 a.m.–5 p.m.; Tuesday 8 a.m.–noon and 4–8 p.m.; Thursday 8 a.m.–8 p.m. Call for walk-in rules and holiday changes.
Jean Yawkey Place clinic
entries.address: Address: 780 Albany Street, first floor, Boston, MA 02118

entries.title: BHCHP dental care
entries.description:
Phone: 857-654-1885.
Dental care for people experiencing homelessness. Urgent walk-in times are published on weekdays in the morning and at 12:30 p.m., with a Thursday late-afternoon session; call because capacity and hours can change.
BHCHP dental services

entries.title: BHCHP shelter clinics
entries.description:
Boston Health Care for the Homeless also operates scheduled clinics in shelters and day programs. Use its current location list to find the nearest service and call before traveling.
BHCHP locations and hours

entries.title: Behavioral Health Help Line
entries.description:
Call or text: 833-773-2445, 24 hours.
Massachusetts' free behavioral-health line connects people to mental-health and substance-use care in more than 200 languages. Insurance is not required. Call 911 for immediate physical danger or a life-threatening medical emergency.
Massachusetts emergency and crisis services

entries.title: PAATHS — access to recovery services
entries.description:
24-hour phone: 855-494-4057. Walk-in hours: Monday–Friday, 7 a.m.–5 p.m.
Assessment, referrals, transportation, and help navigating insurance for substance-use treatment. PAATHS does not itself provide treatment or guarantee a bed.
PAATHS — City of Boston
entries.address: Address: 774 Albany Street, first floor, Boston, MA 02118

entries.title: AHOPE — harm reduction and testing
entries.description:
Phone: 617-534-3974.
Harm-reduction supplies, drug checking, HIV, STI, and hepatitis testing, and referrals. Call for current walk-in hours.
Boston substance-use services guide

entries.title: Massachusetts Substance Use Helpline
entries.description:
Call or text: 800-327-5050, 24 hours.
Free and confidential connection to treatment and recovery services. Ask about detoxification, medication, residential or outpatient care, and transportation. Availability changes daily.
Massachusetts treatment and recovery helplines

entries.title: DTA — SNAP food benefits and cash assistance
entries.description:
DTA Assistance Line: 877-382-2363. Workers are available Monday–Friday, 8:15 a.m.–4:45 p.m.; automated case information is available 24 hours.
Apply for SNAP or TAFDC/EAEDC cash assistance, replace an EBT card, upload documents, or request disability and language accommodations. Press 7 to apply for SNAP. Interpreters are available.
How to contact DTA

entries.title: SNAP when you do not have housing or cooking facilities
entries.description:
Tell DTA that you are homeless and whether you cannot store or cook food. Some households that include an older, disabled, or homeless person may qualify to buy prepared meals from participating restaurants. Eligibility and expedited service require screening.
Apply for SNAP — Massachusetts

entries.title: MassHealth
entries.description:
Customer service: 800-841-2900; TTY: 711. Staff are available Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m.; interpreters are available.
Apply for or manage state health coverage and ask for an enrollment assister. BHCHP can also help patients navigate coverage.
MassHealth application help

entries.title: Boston Housing Authority applications
entries.description:
Status and application help: 617-988-3400, Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–4:30 p.m.
Public, project-based, and other waiting lists use separate online portals. BHA warns that it has no immediate housing and waits can last years; the tenant-based Section 8 list is currently closed. Ask which lists are open and whether you can document a priority.
Apply for BHA housing
entries.address: In-person help: 52 Chauncy Street, Boston, MA 02111

entries.title: Housing search and coordinated services
entries.description:
Ask shelter or day-center case managers for a housing assessment, help collecting homelessness verification, and referrals to supportive or subsidized housing. An assessment is not an immediate housing offer. Keep phone and mailing information current with every program.
Boston housing and shelter resources

entries.title: MassHire Downtown Boston Career Center
entries.description:
Phone: 617-399-3100. Hours: Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; resource center closes at 4 p.m.
Free job-search resources, career counseling, workshops, training information, and computer access. Personalized help may require an appointment.
MassHire Downtown Boston
entries.address: Address: 75 Federal Street, third floor, Boston, MA 02110

entries.title: MassHire Boston ABCD Career Center
entries.description:
Phone: 617-442-2791. Hours: Monday–Thursday, 8:30 a.m.–4:30 p.m.; Friday, 8:30 a.m.–3 p.m.
In-person and virtual job-search support, workshops, and training referrals. Call to confirm an appointment and ask about neighborhood career-adviser sessions.
MassHire Boston ABCD contact and hours
entries.address: Address: 10 Malcolm X Boulevard, Roxbury, MA 02119

entries.title: Project Place
entries.description:
Phone: 617-542-3740.
Case management, resource connections, employment training, and support for people rebuilding stability. Call for orientation, eligibility, and the current program schedule.
Project Place in the City resource directory

entries.title: Serving Ourselves — shelter workforce program
entries.description:
A paid six-month job-training program for people staying in Boston Public Health Commission shelters. Ask shelter staff about eligibility, enrollment, and the next cohort.
Serving Ourselves program — City of Boston
entries.address: Career center: 1010 Massachusetts Avenue, Boston, MA 02118

entries.title: St. Francis House employment services
entries.description:
Career support is available alongside meals, showers, mail, identification, and case management. Ask the day center about orientation, computer access, clothing for interviews, and training.
St. Francis House programs

entries.title: Identification, birth records, and mailing address
entries.description:
Start with St. Francis House, Women's Lunch Place, Rosie's Place, or your shelter case manager. Ask for help obtaining a birth certificate or state ID, paying a required fee, making copies, and establishing a safe mailing address. Requirements differ by record and state.
St. Francis House document and mail help

entries.title: Greater Boston Legal Services
entries.description:
Main: 617-371-1234; housing intake: 617-603-1807.
Free civil legal help for eligible low-income people, including eviction, public or subsidized housing, benefits, health, family, and shelter denials or terminations. General telephone intake is Monday–Friday, 9:30 a.m.–12:30 p.m.; housing intake is by phone.
GBLS hours and intake

entries.title: Rosie's Place Legal Program — women
entries.description:
Legal helpline: 617-318-0271.
Legal support and advocacy for women. Call to learn intake hours and whether the matter can be handled or referred.
Rosie's Place service guide

entries.title: Eviction, shelter denial, or benefits problem
entries.description:
Keep every notice and envelope, photograph it, and record the deadline. Call GBLS promptly. For an emergency family-shelter denial or termination, tell intake that it concerns Emergency Assistance shelter and give the date on the notice.
GBLS housing legal help

categories.title: Women, youth, veterans, LGBTQ+ people, and immigrants

entries.title: SafeLink — domestic violence
entries.description:
Call: 877-785-2020, 24 hours.
Confidential safety planning and connections to domestic-violence shelter and services. In immediate danger, call 911. Do not disclose a safe location to the person causing harm.
Massachusetts SafeLink resources

entries.title: Bridge Over Troubled Waters — ages 14–24
entries.description:
Phone: 617-423-9575.
Overnight shelter and daytime services for young people. Call for current intake, age rules, and capacity.
Boston youth homelessness resources

entries.title: Y2Y Harvard Square — ages 18–24
entries.description:
Phone: 617-864-0795.
Youth shelter outside Boston but accessible by transit. Call for the current lottery or intake process, hours, and capacity.
City youth resource list
entries.address: Address: 1 Church Street, middle entrance, Cambridge, MA 02138

entries.title: BAGLY — LGBTQ+ youth
entries.description:
Phone: 617-227-4313.
Community, advocacy, and programs for LGBTQ+ youth. Call for the current drop-in schedule and ask for housing or health referrals when needed.
BAGLY in Boston's youth resource list

entries.title: New England Center and Home for Veterans
entries.description:
Phone: 617-371-1800.
Housing and supportive services for veterans. Call for shelter or housing intake, eligibility, and documentation. Veterans may also call 211 for additional VA and community referrals.
Veteran shelter listing — City of Boston

entries.title: Mayor's Office for Immigrant Advancement
entries.description:
Phone: 617-635-2980. Hours: Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–5 p.m.
Resource navigation, interpretation and translation access, and referrals for immigrant residents. The office also publishes free brief immigration-law consultations; contact it for the current session and registration.
Resources for immigrant communities
entries.address: Address: 1 City Hall Square, Room 806, Boston, MA 02201

entries.title: FamilyAid — families
entries.description:
Phone: 617-542-7286.
Family homelessness prevention, case management, and resource connections. Call for eligibility and intake; it is not a guaranteed same-day emergency placement.
Family services in Boston's directory

entries.title: Boston Animal Care and Control — pet food and emergencies
entries.description:
Information: 617-635-1800. After-hours animal emergency: 311 or 617-635-4500.
The City runs a year-round pet food pantry, low-cost rabies clinics, and an animal shelter. Call before traveling for pet-food availability, clinic dates, and eligibility.
Boston Animal Care and Control
entries.address: Animal shelter: 26 Mahler Road, Roslindale, MA 02131

entries.title: Low-cost veterinary options
entries.description:
The City lists low-cost clinics, including Merwin Animal Clinic at 542 Cambridge Street, Brighton, 617-782-5420, and the Spay Waggin' at 877-590-7729. Call for prices, appointments, weight limits, and current services.
Boston low-cost animal clinics

entries.title: Before accepting a shelter placement
entries.description:
Tell the shelter or 311 that you have a pet, including the species, size, vaccination status, and any medical need. Ask whether the assigned site can accommodate the animal or arrange a safe alternative. Do not assume every shelter accepts pets.
Boston shelter contacts

entries.title: Sources and updates
entries.description:
This page prioritizes the City of Boston, Commonwealth of Massachusetts, and provider websites. It was reviewed on November 12, 2026. If a phone number is disconnected, an address is wrong, or a service has closed, please submit a correction through the project repository.
How to contribute | Project repository — ../../CONTRIBUTING.md
